newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - Dutch Oce Q3 net profit jumps.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dutch Oce Q3 net profit jumps.

text.p: Oce-van der Grinten, Europe's biggest independent photocopier manufacturer, reported strong third-quarter growth on Wednesday and said it expected this to continue in the current final quarter.
The Dutch group's June-August net profit jumped by 71 percent to 38.9 million guilders from 22.7 million in the same 1995 period.
"For the fourth quarter we expect a continuation of the positive development over the first nine months," it said in a statement.
Net profits for the first nine months showed an increase of 51 percent to 107.5 million guilders.
In early Amsterdam trading, Oce shares put on 3.30 guilders to 196.50 guilders.
Oce said the third-quarter improvement was largely due to the 900 million guilder acquisition in April of HPP, the high-performance printing division of Germany's Siemens Nixdorf .
"The strong increase in operating profit was also due to the contribution made by HPP," it said.

Third-quarter sales rose 61 percent to 1.12 billion guilders. "Disregarding exchange rate effects (plus 5 percent) and the HPP acquisition (plus 41 percent), sales would have increased by 15 percent," it said.
HPP sales in the period to end-August were 288 million guilders. Oce said HPP's results were characterised by a lower gross margin and lower operating costs.
Third-quarter net per share rose to 1.90 guilders from a previous 1.39 guilders. Operating profit increased to 75.5 million guilders from 50.8 million.
Oce will pay an unchanged interim dividend of 0.90 guilders.
Analysts welcomed the sharp profit rise.

"We're very satisfied with the results and comfortable with our estimates for full-year net profit of 164.9 million guilders and net per share of 9.05 guilders," said Bank Labouchere's Ad van der Laar. "We expect further good messages from Oce."
Oce also said it was buying the 80 percent of Swiss engineering and office systems firm Messerli that it did not already control. The takeover will come into effect in January.
The Dutch group has held a 20 percent stake in Messerli since 1989. "Thanks to Messerli's strong market position, Oce products have a high level of brand awareness on the Swiss market," it said.
Messerli has annual sales of 225 million guilders and employs more than 600 staff. No financial details were given on the acquisition.
